# What does this PR do?

Fixes #36683 

Enables `AutoModelForCausalLM` with multimodal checkpoints, to load a decoder-only text model.

E.g. the following now works:
```py
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/gemma-3-4b-it")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("google/gemma-3-4b-it", device_map="auto")

inputs = tokenizer(["The quick brown"], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
gen_out = model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False)
print(tokenizer.batch_decode(gen_out, skip_special_tokens=True))
```
pr_comments: Hi 👋, thank you for opening this pull request! The pull request is converted to draft by default. When it is ready for review, please click the `Ready for review` button (at the bottom of the PR page).

The docs for this PR live [here](https://moon-ci-docs.huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_36741). All of your documentation changes will be reflected on that endpoint. The docs are available until 30 days after the last update.

There are two angles to this question:
1. What we communicate to our users;
2. Whether we should enable it or not.

_______________________
Regarding 1:

In the [release notes](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases) we write "For text-only inputs use Gemma3ForCausalLM for generation to avoid loading the vision tower.", so we expect the model to be used as text-only. Both `gemma3` and `gemma3_text` are in the auto map for `AutoModelForCausalLM`. As such, from our side, we indicate to the user that any `gemma3` model is compatible with `AutoModelForCausalLM`, implicitly (can be used as text-only model) and explicitly (it's part of the auto map).

It is not compatible at the moment, so we must choose whether to enable it or update other parts accordingly (including perhaps exceptions) 🤗 

______________________
Regarding 2:

If `gemma3` supports text-only, I'm deeply in favor of enabling it with `AutoModelForCausalLM`:
- `Gemma3ForCausalLM` is supported, and it is the same (minus the ease of use)
- Many downstream libraries use auto classes and don't want to bother with model-specific imports. It makes their development cycle much easier.
- Without `AutoModelForCausalLM`, the alternative auto class loads the vision tower (= waste of memory)
- The changes are minimal, as we can see in this PR

I don't think we should do it for all combinations of modalities, not unless there is a demand for it. However, text-only generation is the most used task in our library and on the hub, and it is expected that new models will often be text + other modalities. As such, if we don't enable this, downstream libraries/users will have to pick between model-specific imports and additional memory usage.

For me, the advantages are very clear :)

Regarding the communication, I see how there might have been some confusion. The idea was that Gemma3 has a 1B checkpoint trained on text-only, so users are expected to load it with `CausalLM`

> If Gemma3 supports text-only, I'm deeply in favor of enabling it with AutoModelForCausalLM  

I understand the reasoning behind this, but I think we should also consider consistency with other VLMs. Gemma3 and Mllama are only models that have a separate `CausalLM` class. Even though any other VLMs can work in text-only setting with decent quality, we didn't add a `CausalLM` class for them since the models released didn't have a text-only checkpoint. If we decide to introduce `CausalLM` for all models that support text, it would make sense to extend the same approach to other VLMs as well.  

As a reference point, LLaVa users have been running the model in text-only mode by loading `ConditionalModel`, and we’ve enabled it by ensuring the processor doesn’t raise errors when `images=None` which is standard by now for all processors afair

> Without AutoModelForCausalLM, the alternative auto class loads the vision tower (= waste of memory)  

Valid concern, though in practice, the additional memory overhead is relatively small (200-500M params with SigLIP). While not ideal, this may not significantly impact users, especially since they are intentionally choosing a multimodal model for text-only tasks

> Many downstream libraries use auto classes and don't want to bother with model-specific imports. It makes their development cycle much easier

I think this is the strongest argument for adding `CausalLM`. However, I’d like to clarify whether this is an actual limitation of VLLM—where it can't generate from text-only inputs with `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration`—or if this is more about user expectations shaped by our documentation. Given that previous multimodal releases didn’t raise similar concerns, I suspect this is more of a communication issue than technical limitation on VLLM.  

If we decide to add add `CausalLM` for gemma3 multimodal models, we would need to ensure consistency across other model. This shouldn’t be too difficult since part of the standardization process for VLLM already involves separating `BaseModel` and `lm-head` for all multimodals - though it may add some redundancy imho

Would love to hear thoughts on this! If you agree with the above, I would be pro of shaping better our communication next time, and be more explicit on docs. I feel like in general the docs for multimodality lacks a lot of information, but I wanted first to make sure we have a consistent API before adding a section for `Multimodal LLMs`
Thanks a lot for this PR 🙏 . Any chance this can be added to the v4.49.0-Gemma-3 tag? Or is 4.50 around the corner anyway?

>Or is 4.50 around the corner anyway?

yes, it is 😉

issue_context.title: AttributeError: 'Gemma3Config' object has no attribute 'vocab_size'
issue_context.body:
### System Info

v4.50.0.dev0


### Who can help?

@ArthurZucker 
@LysandreJik 
@xenova 

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

I am trying to run the new Gemma3 model, using version '4.50.0.dev0'.

When loading the model I get the error: 'Gemma3Config' object has no attribute 'vocab_size'.

Looking into this it seems Gemma3Config has `vocab_size` nested in a "text_config" attribute. 

I try to load the model as AutoModelForCausalLM, running it with Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration does not raise this issue. Am I wrong in assuming I can run Gemma 3 as AutoModelForCausalLM?

### Expected behavior

Loading the model as AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained without issue.
comments:
I encountered the same issue as well. One might assume that adding `vocab_size` to the model's `config.json` would resolve the problem, especially since there is a `vocab_size` present in [this `config.json`](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-3-1b-it/blob/main/config.json).

However, even after making that adjustment, I faced a multitude of other errors related to missing configuration keys in the transformers loader.

### **The Persistent Challenge: Beyond Vocabulary Size**

The initial error I encountered was a `KeyError` indicating a missing `vocab_size` in the configuration. This issue is merely the *surface* of a more profound systemic problem when loading large transformer models like Gemma in environments such as Text-Generation-WebUI. While adding the missing `vocab_size` resolves the immediate `KeyError`, it does not provide a comprehensive solution; instead, it triggers a cascade of subsequent errors related to *other* missing configuration options. This is not simply a matter of a few isolated omissions; it reflects a fundamental mismatch between the model’s expectations and the configuration capabilities of the environment.

### **The Cascade of Missing Configuration Options**

After addressing the `vocab_size` issue, I began encountering a series of `AttributeError` and `KeyError` exceptions, each necessitating the addition of yet another configuration option. Some of the critical parameters include:

*   **`hidden_size`**: The model requires a specific hidden size, which must be explicitly included in the configuration.
*   **`num_hidden_layers`**: The expected number of hidden layers needs to be defined.
*   **`rope_theta` & `rope_base`**: These parameters are essential for the RoPE implementation and must be present for accurate position embedding calculations.
*   **`intermediate_size`**: This defines the size of the intermediate feed-forward layer within the transformer.
*   **`num_key_value_heads`**: This is crucial for grouped-query attention mechanisms.
*   **`hidden_activation`**: This specifies the activation function used in the hidden layers.
*   **`num_attention_heads`**: This indicates the number of attention heads.

The process quickly becomes a tedious cycle: add one option, trigger another error, add that option, and so forth. Even after meticulously including *all* seemingly necessary configuration parameters, the `Gemma3` model may still fail to load correctly. This is often due to an internal process known as "dynamic model initialization," compounded by the use of "meta tensors."

[edit I see you mentioned this already in your OP. Leaving the workaround here for visibility]

I resolved this error by using Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration per the model card, rather than AutoModelForCausalLM:

```
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration
model = Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    model_id, device_map="auto"
)
```

I'm getting a warning about "The model 'Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration' is not supported for text-generation", but inference works.

@ZipingL , I think the issue is mainly that by using the AutoModel initialization it somehow passes an `Gemma3Config` to the Gemma3TextModel, instead of a `Gemma3TextConfig`, here at L619:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v4.49.0-Gemma-3/src/transformers/models/gemma3/modeling_gemma3.py#L619

All the config args you mention would be in Gemma3Config["text_config"]. Maybe it happens because AutoModel uses AutoConfig to initialize the config, which probably defaults to `Gemma3Config`, instead of `Gemma3TextConfig`?

Edit: Looks like my hunch was right, the `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration` even uses `AutoModelForCausalLM` to initialize the language_model but passes `config.text_config` to it: 
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v4.49.0-Gemma-3/src/transformers/models/gemma3/modeling_gemma3.py#L1120

In [`models/auto/modeling_auto.py`, line 523](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/50d3530a/src/transformers/models/auto/modeling_auto.py#L523) I've tried replacing `Gemma3ForCausalLM` with `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration` and it works for me – Gemma 3 4B successfully loads with `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained`. I'm only interested in text generation though, so not sure if image processing would be affected by this quick fix.
Hugging Face maintainer here: I can reproduce the `'Gemma3Config' object has no attribute 'vocab_size'` error. Raising the issue internally and we'll try to get a fix ASAP!
Is there a way to use the `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration` workaround with vLLM?

Hey all! Yes, Gemma3ForCausalLM cannot be loaded with auto mapping unfortunately, and it is a known limitation. We have it noted, and the reason is that the same hub model-id is loaded with two different tasks in transformers. That in turn causes issues when we try to infer the config type for CausalLM

There could be a dirty workaround, but the idea was to not support AutoModel until a solid solution is available. Loading with `Gemma3ForCausalLM` should work though

Hi folks 👋 

With #36741, which will be included in the next patch release, you can load the text-only part of gemma3 with `AutoModelForCausalLM`:

```py
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("google/gemma-3-4b-it", device_map="auto")
```

Until then, you can do `pip install --upgrade git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git` to install from `main` and unlock this fix.

We apologize for the slower reply: we were discussing a systemic solution for this problem, as we expect it to happen with more modalities in the near future :) #36741 is a band-aid, a more scalable solution is in our plans.

Just to be clear on my configuration.  I am in a docker container (vllm/vllm-openai). Gemma3 was not supported at all. 

In my container :
```

pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers@v4.49.0-Gemma-3

sed -i 's/from vllm import SamplingParams/from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams/g' ./vllm/spec_decode/batch_expansion.py

sed -i 's/from vllm import __version__ /from .version import __version__ /g' ./vllm/vllm/config.py

```
